t: The Arthashastra is a compilation of earlier treatises, revised over centuries, which covers government, law, taxes, trade, spies, diplomacy and war.
Tradition ascribes it to Chanakya, counsellor of Chandragupta Maurya, but studies since 1965 have mostly rejected this, pointing to several authors and to details that fit the first centuries CE.
Thought lost by colonial-era scholars, it was identified in 1905 in the Mysore Oriental Library and published by R. Shamasastry in 1909.
dyk: The text advises that in areas struck by famine, epidemic or war the king should start public projects such as irrigation works and forts, and exempt those affected from taxes. It also recommends feeding horses and elephants that are too old, sick or injured to work.
ev: On Olivelle's dating, the oldest layer, separate treatises by separate authors, begins to be written, between 150 BCE and 50 CE
The Kautilya Recension, probably titled Dandaniti, is compiled between 50 and 125 CE on Olivelle's dating
The Spitzer Manuscript, found near Kizil in China, carries verses of the Arthashastra
The Shastric Redaction, the text as it exists today, is made between 175 and 300 CE on Olivelle's dating
A palm-leaf manuscript given to the Mysore Oriental Library is identified by Rudrapatna Shamasastry as the Arthashastra
Shamasastry publishes the Sanskrit text, followed by the first English translation in 1915
R. P. Kangle publishes a critical edition based on all the available manuscripts
The Arthashastra is inscribed in the UNESCO memory register at the 11th General Meeting of the Memory of the World Committee for Asia and the Pacific

f.made: Several authors over centuries; according to Olivelle, separate source treatises of 150 BCE to 50 CE, a compilation by a person named Kautilya in 50 to 125 CE and a major redaction between 175 and 300 CE; tradition names Chanakya, the counsellor of Chandragupta Maurya
f.form: A Sanskrit treatise, mostly prose with a verse at the end of each chapter, in 15 books, 150 chapters and 180 topics, with about 5,300 sentences on politics, governance and war, apart from the table of contents and the epilogue
f.where: Manuscripts include a palm-leaf copy given to the Mysore Oriental Library, a Malayalam-script manuscript in the Bavarian State Library and a Devanagari manuscript in a Jain library at Patan, Gujarat; early fragments come from sites in China, Afghanistan and Pakistan
f.known: Statecraft and the duties of a king; the sage king; the network of spies; the six-fold policy and the Mandala theory; a mixed economy with taxes and state superintendents; civil and criminal law; the identification with Chanakya and its rejection by scholars
